title: Baseline caching for guardrails eval runs + invalidation on model/prompt-set changes
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
## Context
Optimize Guardrails “apply gating” invokes eval-harness suites before applying cost optimizations (batching/caching/quantization/routing). Without caching, we re-run identical suites for:
- repeated apply attempts
- canary rollouts (same delta across multiple routes)
- UI refresh / “rerun gating” flows

This creates avoidable load, increases time-to-decision, and causes noisy timeouts during peak usage.

## Goal
Implement baseline caching/dedup for eval runs so that *identical* gating requests reuse prior results, with correct invalidation whenever the inputs that could affect quality change.

## Non-goals
- Cross-tenant result sharing (do not reuse results across tenants by default).
- Changing eval-harness scoring/aggregation logic (handled in ENG-3915).

## Proposed design
### 1) Cache key (deterministic)
Cache is keyed by a canonical “eval input fingerprint” derived from:
- tenant_id (required; no cross-tenant reuse)
- model_id + model_version (or immutable digest) used by runtime
- prompt_set_id + prompt_set_revision
- suite_id(s) and suite_version (if suite definitions are versioned)
- gating_mode_version (output schema / aggregation semantics)
- config_delta_fingerprint (normalized representation of the Optimize proposal)
  - quantization: from_profile -> to_profile + any runtime flags
  - batching/caching: batch params, cache policy params
  - routing: policy change inputs
- grader_version(s) (where applicable) and evaluator container/image digest

Normalization requirement: config deltas must be sorted + stable stringified prior to hashing, to avoid “same change, different JSON order” cache misses.

### 2) Storage + TTLs
- Persist eval run summary + key fields in the eval runner DB (source of truth).
- Maintain a fast lookup index from fingerprint -> latest successful run_id in Redis (or equivalent) with TTL.
- TTL proposal:
  - successful results: 7 days (subject to revision invalidation)
  - failures/timeouts: 30–60 minutes (to prevent thundering herd, but allow quick retry after a fix)

### 3) Invalidation rules
Invalidate (i.e., generate a *new fingerprint* and bypass cache) when any of the following changes:
- model_version changes
- prompt_set_revision changes
- suite_id list changes OR suite version changes
- evaluator/grader image digest changes
- gating_mode_version changes (output semantics)
- config_delta_fingerprint changes

Operationally, invalidation is implemented by incorporating these fields into the fingerprint; we do not need an explicit “delete” path for correctness.

### 4) Dedupe / in-flight coalescing
If multiple identical requests arrive concurrently:
- First request creates a run record (status=queued) and writes fingerprint->run_id mapping.
- Subsequent requests should return the existing run_id (and not enqueue duplicate work) while status is queued/running.

Need to handle race conditions:
- use DB unique constraint on fingerprint for “active” runs (or a Redis SETNX lock with short expiry + DB fallback)
- if a run_id exists but is terminal + too old, create a new run

### 5) API behavior
- Optimize apply should receive:
  - cache_hit: true/false
  - reused_run_id (if cache hit)
  - run_created_at (to inform UI “reused results from …”)
- Provide a way to bypass cache for admins / explicit rerun:
  - rerun=true forces a new run (adds a nonce to fingerprint OR bypasses lookup)
  - restricted behind feature flag / RBAC (align with override work)

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Identical gating requests reuse a prior successful result without re-running eval-harness.
- [x] Any change in model version or prompt set revision results in a cache miss (new run).
- [x] Cache key includes evaluator image digest / grader versions to avoid using stale results after harness upgrades.
- [x] In-flight requests are deduped (no duplicate jobs enqueued for same fingerprint).
- [x] Cache hit/miss is emitted to telemetry and visible in dashboards.
- [x] Unit tests cover canonicalization + invalidation scenarios.

## Testing plan
- Unit tests:
  - canonicalization: JSON ordering differences produce same fingerprint
  - model version change produces new fingerprint
  - prompt set revision change produces new fingerprint
  - suite list order normalization (order-independent)
  - rerun=true bypasses reuse
- Integration tests:
  - two concurrent requests for same fingerprint: only one job enqueued
  - cache hit returns prior run_id + does not increase job queue depth

## Notes / edge cases
- Partial results: do not cache partial/errored runs as “successful” results. We may cache failures briefly to reduce repeated timeouts.
- Data retention: caching relies on summaries staying available (ties to retention policy work in later PR).
- Cardinality: fingerprint should not include raw prompts or per-example IDs; only revisions and digests.

## Links
- Related tickets: ENG-3914 (async eval runner), ENG-3915 (gating mode output), ENG-3918 (telemetry/audit)
- Implementation PR: sources/github/redwood/pr_18470.json (caching layer keyed by model version + prompt-set rev + suite + config delta)
comments: 2025-01-21 — Michael Nguyen: Drafted fingerprint fields. Key open question: do we include threshold-policy version? Proposed: yes, include guardrail policy version to avoid reusing results across threshold semantics changes (even if metrics same). Waiting on Product/Applied ML guidance.

2025-01-22 — Selene Huang: +1 include policy schema version, but not the *threshold values* in the cache key unless those values affect suite execution. If thresholds change, we can reuse raw metric aggregates and re-evaluate policy in control plane. (Action: split cache into (a) eval artifacts/metrics and (b) policy decision.)

2025-01-24 — Jordan Lee: Agree with Selene. Let’s cache eval outputs keyed on execution inputs only (model/prompt-set/suite/config delta/evaluator digest). Policy evaluation is deterministic and should be recomputed on read using current policy version. Please ensure the cached record stores metric aggregates + metadata needed for policy evaluation (n, CI, etc.).

2025-01-28 — Olivia Grant: Please include grader image digest in the key; we had a silent behavior change in rubric grader last quarter. Also suggest short TTL for failures/timeouts to avoid “sticky” bad states in pilot.

2025-02-03 — Logan Wright: Telemetry: emit guardrails_eval_cache_hit{tenant_tier, optimization_type, suite_id} but be careful with suite_id cardinality. Prefer suite_group label (e.g., quantization_min, batching_sentinel) and include suite_id only in logs/audit payload.

2025-02-06 — Michael Nguyen: Implemented canonicalization + fingerprinting and in-flight dedupe. Successful cache TTL 7d (Redis index), failure TTL 45m. Added rerun=true param behind feature flag. PR up: redwood#18470.

2025-02-10 — Rafael Mendes (SRE): Ran staging load test with pilot config. Cache hit rate ~62% during repeated applies; queue depth decreased materially. One issue: stale Redis mapping when DB transaction rolls back; please ensure mapping is written after run record commit (or handle missing run on lookup).

2025-02-12 — Michael Nguyen: Fixed Redis write ordering + added fallback: if mapping points to missing run_id, treat as miss and recreate. Added metric guardrails_eval_cache_stale_pointer_total. Marking Done after merge + staging verification.
